Summary

KAN-22: the acceptance matrix A-1…A-26 now runs as executable contract tests. It also includes the classifier-evasion fixture set (D-17 C7) and the review regressions from PR #248 and Fleet #246. In the repository, cases are named by what they do. The plan IDs appear only in this table and on Jira.

- **`mandate/tests/acceptance.toml`:** one row per case, with:
  - the fixture name;
  - literal expected values keyed by situation;
  - the threat and requirement;
  - `pending`, the behaviour the case needs that isn't built yet;
  - the live status.
- **`mandate/tests/test_acceptance.py`:** each fixture drives only the public boundary: `shadow.findings()` (the real diff classifier), `decide()`, `delegation.parse()`, `evidence.normalize()`, and `receipt`/`ledger` against the existing transport fakes.
  - **Statuses:** PASS / PARTIAL / NOT BUILT / FAIL. A row with `pending` items never PASSes.
  - **Unsafe AUTHORIZE:** an AUTHORIZE or a green check where the row expects anything else fails the run by itself.
  - **Stub self-check:** every fixture reruns with `decide()` stubbed to AUTHORIZE, and every row that expects a refusal must then fail.
  - **`--gate`:** exits 0 only when every matrix row passes, i.e. 26/26.
- **Classifier fixes (`mandate/src/mandate/gate.py`):** the evasion set found thirty-five authority changes that would AUTHORIZE once a fact extractor claims "no change". Today's shadow mode only escalates them because it computes no facts.
  - **Parsed comparison (`gate.workflow_changes()`):** each changed workflow is parsed at base and head with PyYAML's safe loader. Duplicate and merge keys are refused. It reports a job whose effective permissions rise (a removed `permissions` block falls back to the repository default; a new workflow starts from none), a new `secrets` read, and a new privileged trigger. An unreadable or unparseable workflow, or a missing parser, fails closed as `permission-added`. The legacy gate compares the PR's merge base with its head, and the merge worker installs PyYAML 6.0.3 with `--require-hashes` from `.claude/skills/merge-gate/requirements.txt` on `ubuntu-24.04`, whose system Python 3.12 has a pinned wheel. Validate Automation Workflows repeats that install on the same runner. The line rules below stay as the fallback for diff-only callers (`judge.py`, self-tests).
  - **Permissions (line fallback):** a workflow line with a bare `write`, a `permissions` key or a YAML alias is a permission change. CodeRabbit showed that a line regex can't follow YAML: an anchored, tagged or aliased value, a merge key, a block scalar or an explicit key each moved the value off its key's line. This also covers the nested flow map and the quoted `'write'` value or `"contents"` key.
  - **Secrets:** a workflow line naming `secrets`, in any case, is a credential. This covers `toJSON(secrets)`, `inputs.token || secrets.X`, an expression split across lines, and `SECRETS.X`.
  - **Comments:** comment lines are skipped, unless they hold `${{`, which GitHub evaluates even inside a script comment.
  - **Values decided elsewhere:** an alias with any anchor name (`*1`) counts, as does a double-quoted value after decoding its escapes (`"wri\x74e"`). So does a line whose value isn't on it: an open double-quoted scalar continued on the next line, or an explicit tag such as `!!binary`.
  - **Moved-in files:** a file renamed into `.github/workflows/` or `.github/actions/` is merge authority, because a rename shows none of its content.
  - **#246:** a Dependabot requirement bump may keep an inline comment, but only unchanged. This replaces the false refusal from KAN-22 comment 10147, and a changed or added comment still refuses.
- **CI:** `validate-workflows.yml` runs the matrix with the other mandate suites. The README documents the matrix and the classifier rules.

Decision: I fixed the classifier here rather than reporting the evasions. KAN-22 requires each evasion to "classify as reserved/ESCALATE; any AUTHORIZE is a hard failure", and the suite can't go into CI while it fails. The alternative I rejected was marking the rows as expected failures, which would hide unsafe AUTHORIZE.

## Scope

- **Not built here:** the components named in "Waits on". Each belongs to later milestones (fact extraction, KAN-28 executor, KAN-23 lifecycle, KAN-31 identities) and is listed on its row as `pending`, so it can't be credited by accident.
- **Permissions:** no permission, credential, ruleset or App change. The workflow changes add test commands, install the hash-pinned parser in the validator, and pin the merge worker and validator to `ubuntu-24.04`.
- **Live gate impact:** `gate.py` is also Fleet's live merge gate, which decides `workflow-change` by evidence and `permission-added`/`credential` by the owner. So on `main` today, each of these evasions lets a workflow PR widen a permission or read secrets without the owner. The changes only flag more lines, except the inline-comment rule, which accepts a bump only when the comment is byte-identical.
- **Undo:** revert the PR.

+"""Acceptance matrix. Run: python3 mandate/tests/test_acceptance.py [--gate]
+
+Each row of acceptance.toml is one positive or adversarial case. Its fixture
+drives only the public Mandate boundary (shadow.findings, decide, delegation,
+evidence, receipt and ledger against the transport fakes) and returns what it
+observed, keyed by situation; the row holds the literal expected values. A
+decision reads "OUTCOME code ...", a check "conclusion title", a refusal
+"refused CODE".
+
+A row is PASS when every value matches and nothing is pending, PARTIAL when
+every value matches but a behaviour it needs is not built yet, NOT BUILT when
+nothing about it is executable yet, and FAIL on any mismatch. Live rows are
+only ever credited by linked run evidence. An AUTHORIZE, a success check or
+the legacy gate's READY where the row expects anything else is unsafe, and
+fails the run on its own.
+
+Exits 0 when no row fails and nothing unsafe was observed; with --gate, only
+when every matrix row also PASSes. A self-check reruns every fixture with
+decide() stubbed to AUTHORIZE and requires each row that expects a refusal to
+fail, so no row can pass without the engine.
+"""

+def diff(path: str, *added: str, removed: tuple[str, ...] = (), old: str | None = None,
+         context: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> str:
+    """A one-hunk unified diff for one file (a rename when ``old`` differs)."""
+    a = old or path
+    body = "".join(f" {x}\n" for x in context) + "".join(f"-{x}\n" for x in removed) + "".join(f"+{x}\n" for x in added)
+    return f"diff --git a/{a} b/{path}\n--- a/{a}\n+++ b/{path}\n@@ -1 +1 @@\n jobs:\n{body}"
+
+
+def findings(text: str, read=lambda path: None) -> tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]:
+    """A diff with no file contents: a workflow in it fails closed."""
+    return shadow.findings(text, [], DELEG, read)
+

+# Workflow fixtures edit this file; the gate parses both versions.
+BASE_WF = (

+    "    steps:\n"

+
+def change(path: str, base: str | None, head: str | None, old: str | None = None):
+    """One file's git diff, with its text at base and at head (None: absent)."""
+    a = old or path
+    header = f"diff --git a/{a} b/{path}\n"
+    header += "new file mode 100644\n" if base is None else "deleted file mode 100644\n" if head is None else ""
+    if a != path:
+        header += ("similarity index 100%\n" if base == head else "") + f"rename from {a}\nrename to {path}\n"
+    body = "".join(difflib.unified_diff((base or "").splitlines(True), (head or "").splitlines(True), f"a/{a}", f"b/{path}"))
+    return header + body, {a: base}, {path: head}
+
+
+def wf(*edits: tuple[str, str], base: str = BASE_WF, path: str = W):
+    """A change to one workflow: each (old, new) replaces text that occurs once."""
+    head = base
+    for old, new in edits:
+        assert head.count(old) == 1, old
+        head = head.replace(old, new)
+    return change(path, base, head)
+
+
+def classify(*changes, read=None, delegation=None) -> tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]:
+    text = "".join(c[0] for c in changes)
+    base = {k: v for c in changes for k, v in c[1].items() if v is not None}
+    head = {k: v for c in changes for k, v in c[2].items() if v is not None}
+    return shadow.findings(text, [], delegation or DELEG, read or base.get, head.get)
+
+
+def said(decision: m.Decision) -> str:
+    return " ".join([decision.outcome, *(x.code for x in decision.reasons)])
+
+
+def decide(found=(("decision-record", "docs/decisions/0001-x.md"),), records=GREEN, *, facts=None,
+           blocking=(), delegation=DELEG, subject=SUBJECT) -> str:
+    return said(m.decide(m.DecisionInput(delegation, subject, tuple(found), dict(NONE if facts is None else facts),
+                                         tuple(records), tuple(blocking))))
+
+
+def refusal(fn) -> str:
+    try:
+        fn()
+    except (l.LedgerError, d.DelegationError) as exc:
+        return f"refused {exc.code}"
+    return "accepted"
+

+def shown(checks: tr.FakeChecks) -> str:

+# A row that runs longer has hung (the gate must answer promptly).
+ROW_SECONDS = 20
+
+
+def _timeout(_signum, _frame):
+    raise TimeoutError(f"row took over {ROW_SECONDS}s")
+

+signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, _timeout)
+# What lets a change through: an AUTHORIZE, a green check, or the legacy gate's READY.
+GRANTS = ("AUTHORIZE", "success", "READY")

+def run(rows: list[dict]) -> list[tuple[dict, dict, str, int]]:
+    results = []
+    for row in rows:
+        signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, ROW_SECONDS)
+        try:
+            observed = FIXTURES[row["fixture"]]()
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - a crash or hang is a failed row, never a pass
+            observed = {"fixture error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"}
+        finally:
+            signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, 0)

+            if v.startswith(GRANTS) and not str(expect.get(k, "")).startswith(GRANTS)

+        if observed != expect:
+            status = "FAIL"
+        elif row.get("pending"):
+            status = "PARTIAL" if expect else "NOT BUILT"
+        else:
+            status = "PASS"
+        results.append((row, observed, status, unsafe))
+    return results

+    return [row["slug"] for row, _, status, _ in results
+            if any(str(v).startswith(refusing) for v in row.get("expect", {}).values()) and status != "FAIL"]

+            print(f"  {status:9} {row['slug']:28} live: {row.get('live', 'not applicable')}"

+            for item in row.get("pending", []):

+            if status == "FAIL":

+                    want, got = row.get("expect", {}).get(k), observed.get(k)
+                    if want != got:
+                        print(f"            {k}: expected {want!r}, observed {got!r}")
+    unsafe = sum(x[3] for x in results)
+    failed = [x[0]["slug"] for x in results if x[2] == "FAIL"]
+    hollow = stub_check(rows)
+    matrix = [x for x in results if x[0]["kind"] == "matrix"]
+    passed = sum(1 for x in matrix if x[2] == "PASS")
+    print(f"\nunsafe AUTHORIZE: {unsafe}; failed rows: {len(failed)}; "
+          f"rows passing with decide() stubbed: {hollow or 'none'}; fixture gate: {passed}/{len(matrix)} matrix rows PASS")
+    ok = not failed and not unsafe and not hollow
+    if "--gate" in argv:
+        ok = ok and passed == len(matrix)
+    print("acceptance " + ("passed" if ok else "FAILED") + (" (fixture gate)" if "--gate" in argv else ""))
+    return 0 if ok else 1

diff --git a/.claude/skills/merge-gate/requirements.txt b/.claude/skills/merge-gate/requirements.txt

index 00000000..cd0611c4
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.claude/skills/merge-gate/requirements.txt
@@ -0,0 +1,12 @@
+# The merge gate parses workflow files to compare effective permissions
+# (mandate.gate.workflow_changes). The merge worker installs this with
+# --require-hashes --only-binary=:all: on ubuntu-24.04, whose system Python is
+# 3.12: the hashes are the CPython 3.12 manylinux wheels (x86_64 for the
+# runner, aarch64 for arm64 containers) and the sdist. Without the parser
+# every workflow change fails closed. Validate Automation Workflows runs the
+# same install on the same runner, so a pin the worker cannot install fails
+# the pull request that changes it.
+pyyaml==6.0.3 \
+    --hash=sha256:ba1cc08a7ccde2d2ec775841541641e4548226580ab850948cbfda66a1befcdc \
+    --hash=sha256:9149cad251584d5fb4981be1ecde53a1ca46c891a79788c0df828d2f166bda28 \
+    --hash=sha256:d76623373421df22fb4cf8817020cbb7ef15c725b9d5e45f17e189bfc384190f
diff --git a/.github/dependabot.yml b/.github/dependabot.yml
index bcd9413a..fc06eb3b 100644
--- a/.github/dependabot.yml
+++ b/.github/dependabot.yml
@@ -123,6 +123,15 @@ updates:
         patterns:
           - "*"
 
+  # The merge gate's workflow parser, which the merge worker installs with
+  # hashes; a bump must update the hashes in the same PR.
+  - package-ecosystem: "pip"
+    directory: "/.claude/skills/merge-gate"
+    schedule:
+      interval: "monthly"
+    commit-message:
+      prefix: "deps"
+
   # The local Git server image is pinned by digest; Dependabot refreshes the
   # base image. Its apk package pins track that base and must be bumped in the
   # same PR; the Template Contract workflow builds the image to catch a miss.

@@ -348,7 +349,29 @@ input is built from:

+  but not in the API's file list still counts. Each changed workflow is also

+  loader; duplicate and merge keys refused), so no spelling, alias, escape,
+  tag or line break can hide what it grants. A job whose effective

+  falls back to the repository default, which may grant write, and a new
+  workflow starts from none. A new expression that reads `secrets` (or a new
+  `secrets: inherit`) is a credential, and a new privileged trigger, or a
+  changed configuration of one (its source workflows, branch or activity
+  filters), is merge authority. A workflow that cannot be read or parsed, a
+  recursive alias, more than 100,000 nodes once aliases are expanded, or a
+  missing parser counts as a permission change. The diff's lines are classified too, as a
+  fallback for callers without file access: a bare `write`, a `permissions`
+  key, an alias, a decoded double-quoted value, an open quote or a tag is a
+  permission change, and a line naming `secrets` is a credential. A file
+  renamed into `.github/workflows/` or `.github/actions/` is merge authority.
+  A Dependabot requirement bump may keep an inline comment, unchanged. The

+  worker installs PyYAML from `.claude/skills/merge-gate/requirements.txt`
+  with hashes, on `ubuntu-24.04`, whose system Python 3.12 has a pinned
+  wheel. Validate Automation Workflows repeats that install on the same
+  runner for every change to the gate, its pins or the workflows.

+# Acceptance matrix for the Mandate decision engine (run: test_acceptance.py).
+#
+# One row per case. Matrix rows follow the acceptance plan's order; evasion rows
+# try to hide an authority change from the scope classifier; regression rows
+# pin defects found in review. Each row's fixture returns what it observed,
+# keyed by situation, and `expect` holds the literal values. `pending` lists
+# behaviour the case needs that is not built yet: such a row never PASSes.
+# `live` is credited only by linked run evidence.
+
+# --- matrix -------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+[[case]]
+slug = "routine-dependency-bump"
+kind = "matrix"
+title = "Authorized routine change: a verified Dependabot patch bump of a pinned action"
+threat = "none: positive control"
+requirement = "a delegated change with proven facts and evidence authorizes"
+fixture = "routine_dependency_bump"
+expect = { "Dependabot provenance" = "version-only", "routine bump with intent evidence" = "AUTHORIZE", "same bump, intent evidence missing" = "VERIFY EVIDENCE_REQUIRED:intent-gate" }
+pending = [
+  "fact extraction: permission, secret and trigger deltas proven from the diff (the fixture supplies them)",
+  "merge executor: merges at the evaluated head and reads the merge back",
+  "lifecycle verification: push workflows ran on the merge commit",
+]
+live = "NOT RUN — gate not reached"
+
+[[case]]
+slug = "missing-runtime-evidence"
+kind = "matrix"
+title = "Missing evidence: admission policy change without runtime acceptance"
+threat = "insufficient evidence"

+"""Acceptance matrix. Run: python3 mandate/tests/test_acceptance.py [--gate]
+
+Each row of acceptance.toml is one positive or adversarial case. Its fixture
+drives only the public Mandate boundary (shadow.findings, decide, delegation,
+evidence, receipt and ledger against the transport fakes) and returns what it
+observed, keyed by situation; the row holds the literal expected values. A
+decision reads "OUTCOME code ...", a check "conclusion title", a refusal
+"refused CODE".
+
+A row is PASS when every value matches and nothing is pending, PARTIAL when
+every value matches but a behaviour it needs is not built yet, NOT BUILT when
+nothing about it is executable yet, and FAIL on any mismatch. Live rows are
+only ever credited by linked run evidence. An AUTHORIZE, a success check or
+the legacy gate's READY where the row expects anything else is unsafe, and
+fails the run on its own.
+
+Exits 0 when no row fails and nothing unsafe was observed; with --gate, only
+when every matrix row also PASSes. A self-check reruns every fixture with
+decide() stubbed to AUTHORIZE and requires each row that expects a refusal to
+fail, so no row can pass without the engine.
+"""
+

+           attempt: int = 1, app: int = e.ACTIONS_APP_ID, policy: str = POLICY) -> e.EvidenceRecord:

+def diff(path: str, *added: str, removed: tuple[str, ...] = (), old: str | None = None,
+         context: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> str:
+    """A one-hunk unified diff for one file (a rename when ``old`` differs)."""
+    a = old or path
+    body = "".join(f" {x}\n" for x in context) + "".join(f"-{x}\n" for x in removed) + "".join(f"+{x}\n" for x in added)
+    return f"diff --git a/{a} b/{path}\n--- a/{a}\n+++ b/{path}\n@@ -1 +1 @@\n jobs:\n{body}"
+
+
+def findings(text: str, read=lambda path: None) -> tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]:
+    """A diff with no file contents: a workflow in it fails closed."""
+    return shadow.findings(text, [], DELEG, read)
+

+# Workflow fixtures edit this file; the gate parses both versions.

+def change(path: str, base: str | None, head: str | None, old: str | None = None):
+    """One file's git diff, with its text at base and at head (None: absent)."""
+    a = old or path
+    header = f"diff --git a/{a} b/{path}\n"
+    header += "new file mode 100644\n" if base is None else "deleted file mode 100644\n" if head is None else ""
+    if a != path:
+        header += ("similarity index 100%\n" if base == head else "") + f"rename from {a}\nrename to {path}\n"
+    body = "".join(difflib.unified_diff((base or "").splitlines(True), (head or "").splitlines(True), f"a/{a}", f"b/{path}"))
+    return header + body, {a: base}, {path: head}
+
+
+def wf(*edits: tuple[str, str], base: str = BASE_WF, path: str = W):
+    """A change to one workflow: each (old, new) replaces text that occurs once."""
+    head = base
+    for old, new in edits:
+        assert head.count(old) == 1, old
+        head = head.replace(old, new)
+    return change(path, base, head)

+def classify(*changes, read=None, delegation=None) -> tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]:
+    text = "".join(c[0] for c in changes)
+    base = {k: v for c in changes for k, v in c[1].items() if v is not None}
+    head = {k: v for c in changes for k, v in c[2].items() if v is not None}
+    return shadow.findings(text, [], delegation or DELEG, read or base.get, head.get)

+def said(decision: m.Decision) -> str:

+def decide(found=(("decision-record", "docs/decisions/0001-x.md"),), records=GREEN, *, facts=None,

+                                         tuple(records), tuple(blocking))))

+def refusal(fn) -> str:
+    try:
+        fn()
+    except (l.LedgerError, d.DelegationError) as exc:
+        return f"refused {exc.code}"
+    return "accepted"

+    return {
+        "the engine moved out": decide(findings(moved("mandate/src/mandate/gate.py", "docs/gate.py"))),
+        "agent instructions moved": decide(findings(moved("AGENTS.md", "docs/agents.md"))),
+        "a ruleset moved": decide(findings(moved(".github/rulesets/main.json", "docs/main.json"))),
+    }
+
+
+@fixture
+def dependabot_inline_comment():
+    def bump(old, new):
+        return diff("requirements.txt", new, removed=(old,))
+
+    commits = [{"author": "dependabot[bot]", "verified": True, "message": "update-type: version-update:semver-patch"}]
+
+    def failures(text):
+        found = gate.dependabot_bump_failures("app/dependabot", "dependabot/pip/requests", commits, text)
+        return "; ".join(found) or "version-only"
+
+    return {
+        "comment kept": failures(bump("requests==2.32.3  # via requests", "requests==2.32.4  # via requests")),
+        "comment changed": failures(bump("requests==2.32.3  # via requests", "requests==2.32.4  # via urllib3")),
+        "comment added": failures(bump("requests==2.32.3", "requests==2.32.4  # via requests")),
+        "package swapped, comment kept": failures(bump("requests==2.32.3  # via requests", "request==2.32.4  # via requests")),
+    }
+
+
+# --- runner -------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+# A row that runs longer has hung (the gate must answer promptly).
+ROW_SECONDS = 20
+
+
+def _timeout(_signum, _frame):
+    raise TimeoutError(f"row took over {ROW_SECONDS}s")
+
+
+signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, _timeout)
+# What lets a change through: an AUTHORIZE, a green check, or the legacy gate's READY.
+GRANTS = ("AUTHORIZE", "success", "READY")
+
+
+def run(rows: list[dict]) -> list[tuple[dict, dict, str, int]]:
+    results = []
+    for row in rows:
+        signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, ROW_SECONDS)
+        try:
+            observed = FIXTURES[row["fixture"]]()
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - a crash or hang is a failed row, never a pass
+            observed = {"fixture error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"}
+        finally:
+            signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, 0)
+        expect = row.get("expect", {})
+        unsafe = sum(
+            1 for k, v in observed.items()
+            if v.startswith(GRANTS) and not str(expect.get(k, "")).startswith(GRANTS)
+        )
+        if observed != expect:
+            status = "FAIL"
+        elif row.get("pending"):
+            status = "PARTIAL" if expect else "NOT BUILT"
+        else:
+            status = "PASS"
+        results.append((row, observed, status, unsafe))
+    return results
+
+
+def stub_check(rows: list[dict]) -> list[str]:
+    """Rows that expect a refusal from decide() but still pass with it stubbed."""
+    real = m.decide
+    m.decide = lambda snapshot: m.Decision("AUTHORIZE", (), (), (), "", snapshot.subject)
+    try:
+        results = run(rows)
+    finally:
+        m.decide = real
+    refusing = ("BLOCK", "ESCALATE", "VERIFY")
+    return [row["slug"] for row, _, status, _ in results
+            if any(str(v).startswith(refusing) for v in row.get("expect", {}).values()) and status != "FAIL"]
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
+    manifest = tomllib.loads(MANIFEST.read_text())
+    rows = manifest["case"]
+    assert len({x["slug"] for x in rows}) == len(rows), "duplicate slug"
+    assert {x["fixture"] for x in rows} == set(FIXTURES), set(FIXTURES) ^ {x["fixture"] for x in rows}
+    results = run(rows)
+    try:
+        commit = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
+    except OSError:  # no git: the report says so rather than failing
+        commit = ""
+    print(f"package {commit or 'unknown'}, manifest sha256:{hashlib.sha256(MANIFEST.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}, "
+          f"registry {m.REGISTRY_VERSION}, fixture policy {POLICY}")
+    for kind in ("matrix", "evasion", "regression"):
+        group = [x for x in results if x[0]["kind"] == kind]
+        print(f"\n{kind}: " + ", ".join(f"{s} {sum(1 for x in group if x[2] == s)}"
+                                       for s in ("PASS", "PARTIAL", "NOT BUILT", "FAIL")) + f" of {len(group)}")
+        for row, observed, status, unsafe in group:
+            print(f"  {status:9} {row['slug']:28} live: {row.get('live', 'not applicable')}"
+                  + (f"  UNSAFE x{unsafe}" if unsafe else ""))
+            for item in row.get("pending", []):
+                print(f"            pending: {item}")
+            if status == "FAIL":
+                for k in sorted(set(observed) | set(row.get("expect", {}))):
+                    want, got = row.get("expect", {}).get(k), observed.get(k)
+                    if want != got:
+                        print(f"            {k}: expected {want!r}, observed {got!r}")
+    unsafe = sum(x[3] for x in results)
+    failed = [x[0]["slug"] for x in results if x[2] == "FAIL"]
+    hollow = stub_check(rows)
+    matrix = [x for x in results if x[0]["kind"] == "matrix"]
+    passed = sum(1 for x in matrix if x[2] == "PASS")
+    print(f"\nunsafe AUTHORIZE: {unsafe}; failed rows: {len(failed)}; "
+          f"rows passing with decide() stubbed: {hollow or 'none'}; fixture gate: {passed}/{len(matrix)} matrix rows PASS")
+    ok = not failed and not unsafe and not hollow
+    if "--gate" in argv:
+        ok = ok and passed == len(matrix)
+    print("acceptance " + ("passed" if ok else "FAILED") + (" (fixture gate)" if "--gate" in argv else ""))
+    return 0 if ok else 1
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

name: Intent Gate

# Runs Infra Fleet Advisor's deterministic checks on the change this pull
# request would merge, and fails when it would newly break a declared
# security, reliability, cost or maintainability position, or hide one the
# advisor could evaluate before. The job itself is defined once, in
# intent-gate-run.yml.

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    # Retargeting without a new commit is gated by intent-gate-retarget.yml.
    # `edited` stays out of this workflow: every title or body edit (bots edit
    # PR bodies) would add a skipped run of this check on the same commit, and
    # with cancel-in-progress could cancel a real run and leave only the skip.
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: intent-gate-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

  intent:
    name: Intent gate
    uses: ./.github/workflows/intent-gate-run.yml

name: Intent Gate (shared)

# The one definition of the Intent Gate job, called by intent-gate.yml for new
# and updated pull requests and by intent-gate-retarget.yml for pull requests
# retargeted to main. The advisor pin lives only here. Read-only: nothing is
# applied, published or commented; the verdict is the check, the evidence is
# the job summary. See the advisor's PDR 0007.

on:
  workflow_call:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  gate:
    name: Declared intent
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Checkout the merge result with history
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      # The pull_request merge commit's first parent is the base as it would be
      # merged, so the comparison covers exactly what this change lands.
      - name: Resolve the compared commits
        id: commits
        run: |
          echo "base=$(git rev-parse HEAD^1)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "head=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # Pinned by SHA: upgrading the advisor is an ordinary reviewed change here.
      - name: Compare declared intent at base and merge result
        uses: ImranAdan/infra-fleet-advisor-public/.github/actions/intent-gate@770a258a423c17ec4c3ca0cacb25b4c842eec6d0
        with:
          base-sha: ${{ steps.commits.outputs.base }}
          head-sha: ${{ steps.commits.outputs.head }}

name: Autonomous merge

# Trusted default-branch code periodically evaluates opted-in, same-repository
# pull requests. The merge gate remains the only authority and binds a merge to
# the exact head it evaluated. PARK, JUDGE and BLOCKED remain open.
on:
  # Wake at the universal gate and the workflows that can be the last
  # applicable check for their path class. External status/review events wake
  # the worker after hosted reviewers finish. The gate still decides every run.
  workflow_run:
    workflows:
      - Intent Gate
      - Advisor remediation validation
      - Infrastructure Validation
      - K8s Manifest Validation
      - Load Harness CI
      - Template Contract
      - Validate Automation Workflows
    types: [completed]
  status:
  schedule:
    # Recovery only; normal merges are event-driven.
    - cron: "7 */6 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      priority_pr:
        description: Pull request to evaluate first
        required: false
        type: string

permissions:
  actions: read
  checks: read
  contents: write
  issues: read
  pull-requests: write
  statuses: read

concurrency:
  group: autonomous-merge
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # mandate: no-receipts (it records no Mandate receipts yet; drop
    # this before the merge worker records, see mandate/README.md)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Check out trusted merge code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Test the candidate selector and merge gate
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/autonomous_merge.py --self-test
          python3 .claude/skills/merge-gate/merge_ready.py --self-test

      - name: Merge evidence-approved pull requests
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          AUTONOMOUS_MERGE_MIN_AGE_SECONDS: "0"
          AUTONOMOUS_MERGE_RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          AUTONOMOUS_MERGE_PRIORITY_PR: ${{ inputs.priority_pr || github.event.workflow_run.pull_requests[0].number || '' }}
          AUTONOMOUS_MERGE_PRIORITY_SHA: ${{ github.event_name == 'status' && github.event.sha || '' }}
        run: python3 .github/scripts/autonomous_merge.py

name: Validate Automation Workflows

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '.github/workflows/**'
      - '.claude/skills/merge-gate/**'
      - 'mandate/**'

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  validate-workflows:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
      
      - name: Validate YAML syntax
        run: |
          echo "🔍 Validating workflow YAML syntax..."

          # Keep tooling deterministic; dependency updates are reviewed here.
          pip install yamllint==1.37.1 --quiet --break-system-packages

          # Create permissive yamllint config (focus on syntax, not style)
          echo "extends: relaxed" > /tmp/yamllint.yml
          echo "rules:" >> /tmp/yamllint.yml
          echo "  trailing-spaces: disable" >> /tmp/yamllint.yml
          echo "  line-length: disable" >> /tmp/yamllint.yml
          echo "  new-line-at-end-of-file: disable" >> /tmp/yamllint.yml

          # Validate each workflow file
          for file in .github/workflows/*.yml; do
            echo "Checking: $file"
            if yamllint -c /tmp/yamllint.yml "$file"; then
              echo "✅ $file - Valid YAML syntax"
            else
              echo "❌ $file - Invalid YAML syntax"
              exit 1
            fi
          done

          echo "✅ All workflow files have valid YAML syntax"

      - name: Validate GitHub Actions syntax
        run: |
          echo "🔍 Validating GitHub Actions workflow syntax..."

          # Download a fixed actionlint release and verify the publisher's
          # checksum before executing it.
          curl --fail --silent --show-error --location \
            --output /tmp/actionlint.tar.gz \
            https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint/releases/download/v1.7.9/actionlint_1.7.9_linux_amd64.tar.gz
          echo "233b280d05e100837f4af1433c7b40a5dcb306e3aa68fb4f17f8a7f45a7df7b4  /tmp/actionlint.tar.gz" | sha256sum --check
          tar -xzf /tmp/actionlint.tar.gz -C /tmp actionlint

          # Run actionlint on all workflow files (disable shellcheck for now)
          if /tmp/actionlint -shellcheck= .github/workflows/*.yml; then
            echo "✅ All workflows have valid GitHub Actions syntax"
          else
            echo "❌ GitHub Actions syntax validation failed"
            echo ""
            echo "Common issues:"
            echo "  - Invalid expression syntax in workflow variables"
            echo "  - Unknown workflow keys or job properties"
            echo "  - Invalid action references"
            echo "  - Type mismatches in workflow configuration"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Self-test merge gate and judge
        run: |
          python3 .claude/skills/merge-gate/merge_ready.py --self-test
          python3 mandate/tests/test_delegation.py
          python3 mandate/tests/test_evidence.py
          python3 mandate/tests/test_decision.py
          python3 mandate/tests/test_shadow.py
          python3 mandate/tests/test_ledger.py
          python3 mandate/tests/test_receipt.py
          python3 .claude/skills/merge-gate/judge.py --self-test

      - name: Check PR workflow changes
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "🔍 Analyzing workflow changes in this PR..."

          # Get list of changed workflow files
          CHANGED_FILES=$(gh pr view ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} --json files --jq '.files[].path' | grep '^.github/workflows/' || true)

          if [ -z "$CHANGED_FILES" ]; then
            echo "ℹ️ No workflow files changed in this PR"
          else
            echo "📝 Changed workflow files:"
            echo "$CHANGED_FILES"
            echo ""
            echo "✅ These files have been validated by actionlint above"
          fi
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

      - name: Check workflow permissions
        run: |
          echo "🔍 Checking workflow permissions and safety..."
          
          # Check for destructive operations
          if grep -r "terraform destroy" .github/workflows/; then
            echo "⚠️ Found destructive operations in workflows"
            echo "🛡️ Safety measures in place:"
            echo "  - Context preservation before destruction"
            echo "  - Forced cleanup of remaining resources"
            echo "  - Automatic state logging"
            echo "  - Manual rebuild only (no auto-rebuild)"
          fi
          
          echo ""
          echo "✅ Workflow validation complete"
          echo "📚 Deployment setup and manual lifecycle steps: CONFIGURATION.md"

  cancel-in-progress: true

name: Intent Gate (retarget)

# A pull request retargeted to main without a new commit produces only an
# `edited` event. This workflow gates that case under its own check name and
# concurrency group, so ordinary title and body edits never add a skipped run
# of, or cancel, the main Intent Gate check. Same job: intent-gate-run.yml.

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    types: [edited]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  intent:
    name: Intent gate (retargeted)
    if: github.event.changes.base != null
    # Job-level, so a later title or body edit (whose job is skipped) cannot
    # cancel a retarget gate that is still running; only another retarget can.
    concurrency:
      group: intent-gate-retarget-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    uses: ./.github/workflows/intent-gate-run.yml

name: Intent Gate (shared)

# The one definition of the Intent Gate job, called by intent-gate.yml for new
# and updated pull requests and by intent-gate-retarget.yml for pull requests
# retargeted to main. The advisor pin lives only here. Read-only: nothing is
# applied, published or commented; the verdict is the check, the evidence is
# the job summary. See the advisor's PDR 0007.

on:
  workflow_call:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  gate:
    name: Declared intent
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Checkout the merge result with history
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      # The pull_request merge commit's first parent is the base as it would be
      # merged, so the comparison covers exactly what this change lands.
      - name: Resolve the compared commits
        id: commits
        run: |
          echo "base=$(git rev-parse HEAD^1)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "head=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # Pinned by SHA: upgrading the advisor is an ordinary reviewed change here.
      - name: Compare declared intent at base and merge result
        uses: ImranAdan/infra-fleet-advisor-public/.github/actions/intent-gate@770a258a423c17ec4c3ca0cacb25b4c842eec6d0
        with:
          base-sha: ${{ steps.commits.outputs.base }}
          head-sha: ${{ steps.commits.outputs.head }}

name: Intent Gate

# Runs Infra Fleet Advisor's deterministic checks on the change this pull
# request would merge, and fails when it would newly break a declared
# security, reliability, cost or maintainability position, or hide one the
# advisor could evaluate before. The job itself is defined once, in
# intent-gate-run.yml.

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    # Retargeting without a new commit is gated by intent-gate-retarget.yml.
    # `edited` stays out of this workflow: every title or body edit (bots edit
    # PR bodies) would add a skipped run of this check on the same commit, and
    # with cancel-in-progress could cancel a real run and leave only the skip.
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: intent-gate-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  intent:
    name: Intent gate
    uses: ./.github/workflows/intent-gate-run.yml

# --require-hashes --only-binary=:all: on ubuntu-24.04, whose system Python is

# runner, aarch64 for arm64 containers) and the sdist. Without the parser
# every workflow change fails closed. Validate Automation Workflows runs the
# same install on the same runner, so a pin the worker cannot install fails
# the pull request that changes it.

delegation.text:
# Delegation for ImranAdan/infra-fleet-public (lives in ImranAdan/mandate-delegation
# at repositories/infra-fleet-public.toml). Version 1 mirrors the evidence deciders
# in Fleet's decision policy; everything that policy sends to the owner escalates.
version = 1
repository = "ImranAdan/infra-fleet-public"
mode = "shadow"      # decide and record only; nothing merges on this file's authority
owner = "ImranAdan"  # the human principal; agents must use other identities
agents = []          # filled in once agent identities are separated from the owner

# Producers: check name + workflow path + event bind authenticity.
[evidence.intent-gate]
check = "Intent gate / Declared intent"
workflow = ".github/workflows/intent-gate.yml"
event = "pull_request"

[evidence.intent-gate-retargeted]
check = "Intent gate (retargeted) / Declared intent"
workflow = ".github/workflows/intent-gate-retarget.yml"
event = "pull_request"

# First match wins per finding; an unmatched finding escalates.
[[classes]]
id = "dependency-pinned"
match = { category = "dependency" }
decide = "authorize"
require = ["intent-gate"]
recovery = "R0"

[[classes]]
id = "dependency-manifest"
match = { category = "dependency-manifest", lockfile_sibling = true }
decide = "authorize"
require = ["intent-gate"]
recovery = "R0"

[[classes]]
id = "workflow-routine"
match = { category = "workflow", permission_delta = "none", secret_delta = "none", trigger_delta = "none" }
decide = "authorize"
require = ["intent-gate"]
recovery = "R0"

[[classes]]
id = "permission-narrowing"
match = { category = "permission-removed" }
decide = "authorize"
require = ["intent-gate"]
recovery = "R0"

[[classes]]
id = "decision-prose"
match = { category = ["decision-record", "product-requirements"] }
decide = "authorize"
require = ["intent-gate"]
recovery = "R0"

[[classes]]
id = "reserved"  # never delegable in version 1
match = { category = ["intent-policy", "credential", "permission-added", "iam", "permanent-infrastructure", "migration", "merge-authority", "delegation", "enforcement"] }
decide = "escalate"
